top_cited_works.title: Comparative analysis of the energetic performance of wood-fiber insulated panels in North American climates
top_cited_works.abstract: Improving the energy efficiency of buildings is one of the most influential actions that can be taken to reduce life cycle energy costs and mitigate building and construction related environmental impacts. This can be done through the use of off-site panelized construction methods, which offer greater safety, efficiency, and speed than conventional building practices. Wood-fiber insulated panels (WIPs) are a family of prefabricated wall and roof panels for modular (new construction) and retrofit applications. These multi-component assemblies utilize wood fiber insulation as a core material adhesively bonded to engineered wood composite faces. A series of whole building energy models have been developed and simulated using EnergyPlus to assess the thermal performance and energy efficiency of buildings constructed with WIPs. Models were developed for single- and multi-family benchmark buildings representing minimum code requirements for residential applications in eight U.S. climate zones, ranging from hot and humid to subarctic conditions, and seven International Energy Conservation Code iterations.
